result.topic_en: Gauss sets up two formulas (Gauss's method for determining an orbit from two radii vectors and the included angle) relating the ratio y of sector to triangle with the eccentric anomaly difference, defines the constants A, B, C, and works a numerical example.
result.transcription:
Litt. E
37 [-51-]

Zwei formeln
1) $\sin\frac14\varepsilon^2 = \frac{-\sin\frac14\delta^2 - \frac14\left(\sqrt[4]{\frac{r'}{r}}-\sqrt[4]{\frac{r}{r'}}\right)^2 + \frac{\sqrt{rr'}\sin\frac12\delta^2}{2p}}{\cos\frac12\delta} = \frac{\frac{uu}{8(rr')^{\frac32}\cos\frac12\delta^2 yy} - \sin\frac14\delta^2 - \tang 2\psi^2}{\cos\frac12\delta}$
$= \frac{uu}{8(rr')^{\frac32}\cos\frac12\delta^3\, yy} -$
[-...-] +
2) $y = 1 + \frac{uu}{6(rr')^{\frac32}}\cdot\frac{1}{yy}\cdot\frac{1}{\cos\frac12\delta^3}\cdot\frac{\varepsilon-\sin\varepsilon}{\frac43\sin\frac12\varepsilon^3}$

$u\sqrt{p} = yrr'\sin\delta$

Man hat also folgende zwei formeln
I $\begin{cases} Ay = \cos W \\ B\tang W = \sin\frac14\varepsilon\end{cases}$
II. $1 + \frac{C}{yy}\cdot\frac{\varepsilon-\sin\varepsilon}{\sin\frac12\varepsilon^3} = y$

Die Constanten A, B, C werden folgendermaassen bestimmt
$C = \frac{uu}{8(rr')^{\frac32}\cos\frac12\delta^3}$
$\sqrt[4]{\frac{r'}{r}} = \cos(45^\circ+\psi)$
$\frac{\tang 2\psi}{\sin\frac14\delta} = \tang\chi$
$\frac{\sin\frac14\delta}{\cos\chi\sqrt{\cos\frac12\delta}} = B$
$A = \frac{B}{\sqrt{C}}$
Wird $Ay=1$ so hat man schlechthin
$1+\frac{4C}{3yy} = y$
Ist aber $Ay>1$ so mache man

$\sin\frac14\varepsilon^2 = \frac{BB}{AAyy} - BB$
$= \frac{C}{yy} - BB$
$p = \frac{4[?] rr'r'\sin\delta^2}{uu(BB+\sin\frac14\varepsilon^2)}$
